claims.sentence: Both osteoarthritis (OA) and rheumatoid arthritis (RA) are types of arthritis, and both cause joint pain and stiffness.
claims.evidence: NHS OA page: condition that makes joints painful and stiff; RA page: swollen, stiff, painful joints; arthritis page covers both

claims.sentence: Because of that overlap, people sometimes assume they are the same condition.
claims.evidence: No retrieved text says people assume they are the same

claims.sentence: They are not.
claims.evidence: OA and RA described as distinct conditions with different mechanisms (cartilage breakdown vs autoimmune)

claims.sentence: They have different causes, tend to affect different joints and are treated differently.
claims.evidence: OA: knees, hips, hand joints; RA: autoimmune, usually both sides, hands and feet; different treatments (lifestyle/pain relief vs DMARDs)

claims.sentence: Osteoarthritis is a condition that makes joints painful and stiff.
claims.evidence: NHS: osteoarthritis is a condition that makes joints painful and stiff

claims.sentence: The NHS says it is the most common type of arthritis in the UK.
claims.evidence: NHS: the most common form of arthritis in the UK

claims.sentence: The protective cartilage on the ends of the bones gradually breaks down.
claims.evidence: Cartilage breakdown not in the excerpts retrieved this pass; undisputed general fact

claims.sentence: The NHS says the exact cause is not known, but several things are thought to raise the risk, and age is one of them.
claims.evidence: 'Exact cause not known' not retrieved; retrieved risk factors: age, obesity, being female, joint injury, family history
claims.newSentence: The NHS lists several things that raise the risk of osteoarthritis, including age, joint injury, extra weight, being female and family history.

claims.sentence: It most often causes problems in the knees, hips and small joints of the hands.
claims.evidence: Almost any joint can be affected but most often knees, hips and small joints of the hands

claims.sentence: Symptoms can be mild and come and go, or be more constant and severe.
claims.evidence: 'Mild and come and go' not retrieved; retrieved: condition does not necessarily get worse over time
claims.newSentence: The NHS says osteoarthritis does not necessarily get any worse over time.

claims.sentence: Rheumatoid arthritis is a long-term condition that causes pain, swelling and stiffness in the joints, usually in the hands, feet and wrists.
claims.evidence: Long-term autoimmune condition; hands and feet most often involved; 'wrists' not retrieved
claims.newSentence: Rheumatoid arthritis is a long-term condition that causes swollen, stiff and painful joints, most often in the hands and feet.

claims.sentence: It is an autoimmune disease: the immune system attacks the lining of the joints.
claims.evidence: Immune system attacks the cells lining the joints

claims.sentence: The NHS says it usually affects joints on both sides of the body, and that morning stiffness often lasts longer than it does in osteoarthritis.
claims.evidence: Typically both sides of the body; morning stiffness often lasts longer than the 30 minutes typical of OA (NICE: prolonged morning stiffness points away from OA)

claims.sentence: Some people also have tiredness, a fever or weight loss.
claims.evidence: Fatigue, fever, sweating, poor appetite, weight loss can occur

claims.sentence: The trigger is not clear, but a higher risk is linked with being female, having a family history of the condition and smoking.
claims.evidence: Unclear trigger; being a woman, family history, smoking raise risk

claims.sentence: For osteoarthritis, the NHS recommends regular exercise, keeping to a healthy weight, suitable footwear and aids that reduce strain on the joint.
claims.evidence: Healthy weight, regular exercise, shock-absorbing footwear, aids such as tap turners

claims.sentence: More severe symptoms may need painkillers and a structured exercise plan with a physiotherapist.
claims.evidence: 'More severe symptoms' not retrieved; retrieved: pain-relief medicines, and physiotherapists/occupational therapists give structured exercise plans and advice on aids
claims.newSentence: Medicines can be used to relieve the pain of osteoarthritis, and physiotherapists and occupational therapists can provide structured exercise plans and advice on aids.

claims.sentence: Surgery to repair, strengthen or replace a damaged joint is considered in some cases where other treatments have not helped.
claims.evidence: Retrieved: surgery generally considered when other treatments are not enough; hip and knee replacement most common; 'repair, strengthen' not retrieved
claims.newSentence: Surgery, most often a hip or knee replacement, is generally considered when other treatments are not enough.

claims.sentence: Rheumatoid arthritis is treated with medicines that slow the disease and reduce inflammation, known as disease-modifying drugs, sometimes alongside biological treatments.
claims.evidence: DMARDs main medicines; biological treatments added when DMARDs alone are not enough; reduce inflammation, slow joint damage

claims.sentence: Painkillers and steroids can ease symptoms, and physiotherapy and occupational therapy are part of care.
claims.evidence: Painkillers, NSAIDs and short-term steroids; physiotherapy and occupational therapy

claims.sentence: With treatment it is possible to reduce the number of flares and limit long-term joint damage.
claims.evidence: Retrieved: treatment can reduce inflammation, relieve pain, prevent or slow joint damage; 'flares' not retrieved
claims.newSentence: There is no cure, but treatment can help to reduce inflammation, relieve pain and prevent or slow joint damage.

claims.sentence: A GP asks about symptoms and examines the joints.
claims.evidence: GP asks about symptoms and examines the joints (OA diagnosis)

claims.sentence: Osteoarthritis can often be diagnosed from the symptoms and an examination.
claims.evidence: NHS/NICE: OA usually diagnosed from history and examination; X-rays/blood tests not usually needed

claims.sentence: For suspected rheumatoid arthritis, blood tests that look for inflammation are used, and the site's pages on CRP and ESR explain two of them.
claims.evidence: NHS RA diagnosis: ESR and CRP inflammation markers among blood tests; meta part harmless

claims.sentence: The laboratory report shows the reference range used.
claims.evidence: Nothing retrieved about reference ranges on reports

claims.sentence: Imaging such as X-rays or ultrasound may also be arranged.
claims.evidence: NHS: scans (X-rays standard) may check for joint inflammation and damage; NICE found ultrasound evidence too limited for routine use
claims.newSentence: Scans such as X-rays may be done to check for joint inflammation and damage.

claims.sentence: A GP appointment is the usual route for joint pain, swelling or stiffness that does not settle.
claims.evidence: See a GP for unexplained pain, swelling or stiffness in joints that does not go away in a few days

claims.sentence: The NHS emphasises that early diagnosis and treatment of rheumatoid arthritis can help to prevent joint damage.
claims.evidence: Seeing a GP early: early treatment can prevent it getting worse and reduce risk of joint damage

claims.sentence: If a joint becomes suddenly hot, red and very painful, or there is a fever with a painful joint, the person should contact NHS 111 or the GP the same day.
claims.evidence: NHS: ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if skin around a joint is red or hot, or sore joints with a high or low temperature; 'same day' and 'sudden/very painful' wording not on the page
claims.newSentence: If the skin around a joint is red or hot, or sore joints come with a high or low temperature, the NHS advises asking for an urgent GP appointment or getting help from NHS 111.

claims.sentence: Severe symptoms such as sudden inability to move a limb need 999.
claims.evidence: 999 advice for sudden inability to move a limb not retrieved

claims.sentence: Osteoarthritis is the most common type of arthritis in the UK and mostly affects the knees, hips and small joints of the hands.
claims.evidence: OA most common arthritis; knees, hips, hand joints

claims.sentence: Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune condition in which the immune system attacks the lining of the joints.
claims.evidence: Immune system attacks cells lining the joints

claims.sentence: Rheumatoid arthritis usually affects joints on both sides of the body and brings long morning stiffness, as well as tiredness.
claims.evidence: Both sides of the body, morning stiffness longer than OA, fatigue

claims.sentence: Osteoarthritis is managed with exercise, weight management and pain relief; rheumatoid arthritis needs medicines that reduce inflammation.
claims.evidence: OA: exercise, healthy weight, pain-relief medicines; RA: DMARDs reduce inflammation

claims.sentence: Early assessment matters for rheumatoid arthritis, so a GP appointment is the first step for persistent joint swelling or stiffness.
claims.evidence: See a GP for joint symptoms that persist; early treatment reduces joint damage

claims.sentence: Osteoarthritis is wear in the joint cartilage; rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune condition that inflames the joint lining.
claims.evidence: 'Wear in cartilage' not retrieved this pass; autoimmune part supported
claims.newSentence: Osteoarthritis is a condition that makes joints painful and stiff; rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune condition in which the immune system attacks the lining of the joints.

notes: Evidence is from search summaries naming NHS/NICE pages; URLs attribute by page title. Ultrasound for RA diagnosis is not routinely recommended per NICE evidence review, so removed. The morning-stiffness comparison rests on the summary's 30-minute OA figure plus NICE; avoid quoting the figure.
